newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Telstra raises expenditure target.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Telstra raises expenditure target.

text.p: Australian government-owned telecoms carrier Telstra Corp said on Tuesday it would spend a total of A$20 billion on goods and services by 1997, doubling the initial target of A$10 billion set in 1992.
The company said in a statement it would also spend A$12 billion on future capital projects in the next three years.
Group managing director for network and technology, Doug Campbell, said Telstra had spent a record A$3.1 billion on goods and services in the 1995/96 year.
He said competition was the key reason for the increase in expenditure.
"Telstra is now four years into its five-year industry development plan and has already hit the A$15.5 billion mark, by far exceeding its initial expectations," Campbell said in a statement.
"We are on track to spend A$20 billion for the purchase of goods and services by 1997."
Campbell said the strong outlook for the industry after deregulation in 1997 supported the company's plan to outlay A$12 billion on capital projects over the next three years.

"Growth and innovation resulting from increased competition will continue to boost business opportunities for local industry, particularly in the value-added, content-based services for emerging technologies," he said.
He said Telstra had spent a total of A$4.8 billion on all goods and services in the 1995/96 year.
The Australian government hopes to sell one-third of Telstra for an estimated A$8.0 billion. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273 2730
